transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-17
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rachel (NovusHealth Procurement), Jonas (NovusHealth Security), Priya (NovusHealth Legal)

Summary: quick governance + pricing checkpoint before procurement pathing. Customer wants to align MSA redlines, DPA residency clauses, SLA credits, and privileged access (KMS/SSO) requirements; also confirm Dedicated pricing SKU for trial.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA/data residency, SLA tiers and credits, KMS/HSM options, SSO/SAML + RBAC, pilot capacity/pricing, next legal-to-legal sync

Transcript body:
[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call, then we'll jump in. I'm Aisha, AE on the account. Liam's here from se to run the technical bits.
[00:18] Rachel: Thanks, Aisha. Rachel here. We're trying to close procurement gating this month so wanted to run through any blockers.
[00:25] Liam: hey, hi all. Got a slim deck and some links to the SOC2 and the KMS guide. I'll share after.
[00:33] Priya: Great. I have a handful of DPA clauses to confirm, and Jonas will cover the key management stuff.
[00:39] Jonas: yep. We care about in-flight encryption, customer-managed keys, and proof of key isolation for dedicated deployments.
[00:47] Aisha: Understood. Quick agenda: 1) MSA redline status, 2) DPA and residency, 3) SLA and pricing for dedicated pilot, 4) KMS/SSO details, 5) next steps. Sound ok?
[00:56] Rachel: good.
[00:58] Aisha: Okay first, MSA. We sent our standard MSA with a couple of optional enterprise clauses. Priya, did you get a chance to look?
[01:06] Priya: Yes we reviewed. There are three asks: indemnity cap language, subprocessor notification window, and a narrower data use clause. We also flagged a need for audit rights wording on the hosting environment.
[01:19] Aisha: That's helpful. On indemnity, we typically propose mutual caps tied to fees; for enterprise deals we can take bespoke language but need approval from legal. We can include a short exception note if needed.
[01:31] Priya: Ok. If you can send a redline showing mutual cap at X and the subprocessor notice to 30 days that would help.
[01:40] Aisha: Sure, we'll pull that together.
[01:43] [01:45] Speaker 2: (background) sorry, just dropped a link to the pricing sheet in chat.
[01:50] Liam: Cool, I shared the SOC2 summary and a high level architecture diagram in the chat too, link at the end of the transcript.
[01:58] Rachel: On the residency piece — NovusHealth has PHI-ish data and certain EU patient records; we need to confirm hosting region constraints and egress controls. Which deployment options let us fully control residency?
[02:11] Liam: Two options: Hosted with region pinning for most traffic, or Dedicated/Private where the customer can select region and we can offer VPC peering or on-prem package. For strict residency and PHI, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[02:26] Jonas: For Dedicated we still need clarity on whether KMS is customer-managed (BYOK) and if HSM-backed keys are possible. Also key rotation and ephemeral access for SE debugging is a big ask.
[02:38] Aisha: We support BYOK for Private deployments; Dedicated has an option to integrate with customer KMS. We have an HSM integration path on request — that's part of the enterprise package. Liam, can you confirm what we would need for evidence?
[02:50] Liam: Yes. We can provide an integration guide and a short compliance attestation for the HSM flow. For key rotation, our runtime honors KMS rotation, and we namespace keys per-customer so isolation is enforced. We'll provide logs for key usage.
[03:04] Jonas: The key usage logs are critical. We also need assurance that logs won't include plaintext data or tokens.
[03:10] Liam: We never log plaintext inputs; logs show request IDs, token counts, timestamps, model variant. That's the normal pattern.
[03:19] Priya: Good. On the DPA side, we want language that prohibits model training on customer data and clarifies retention windows.
[03:26] Aisha: Redwood's standard DPA includes a non-training clause but we can make it explicit. We can also set retention windows per contract.
[03:33] Rachel: Ok, what's the path for SLA credits? We're used to 99.9 for API uptime with credits tied to token throughput or request latency. How do you measure?
[03:43] Liam: We measure per-route latency, 99.9 vs 99.95 tiering. Credits are prorated based on affected route minutes. For Dedicated, we have a different SLA matrix — more predictable throughput and tighter latency SLOs.
[03:56] Aisha: For pricing, Dedicated baseline is a monthly commitment with a per-hour pool; we'll share a sample SKU. For pilot we can do a short-term reduced commitment to run benchmarks.
[04:07] Rachel: That helps. Do you have a published pricing sheet for the dedicated pool? The one in chat looked like a draft.
[04:13] Aisha: The sheet Liam dropped is draft; we'll convert to a pilot-specific quote and include burn-rate examples for token volumes.
[04:20] Jonas: On privileged access: we need to limit SE access to ephemeral sessions; no standing admin keys. How do you handle escalation for debug?
[04:29] Liam: We use ephemeral session tokens and just-in-time (JIT) access with approvals logged. For private installs we can require VPN or bastion sessions and 2-person approval. We can document the exact escalation workflow.
[04:40] Priya: Can you commit to keeping customer-managed KMS keys entirely under the customer's control? We don't want any copy of keys in vendor systems.
[04:47] Liam: With BYOK for Private, Redwood never persists raw key material; we integrate via KMS APIs and use envelope encryption patterns. We'll provide the integration spec.
[04:58] [05:00] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[05:03] Rachel: About audits — we need a clause for periodic evidence of security posture, not full on-site audits but either third-party attestation or SOC2 report plus a security questionnaire.
[05:15] Aisha: We can provide SOC2 Type II plus a standard security questionnaire. For more formal audit rights we typically scope that in the MSA — open to limited audit rights with notice windows.
[05:26] Priya: We'll draft proposed language and send that to you.
[05:30] Aisha: Great. On the timeline, is procurement hoping to get contract signed this month?
[05:34] Rachel: Ideally yes, pending legal redlines. If legal-to-legal goes smoothly we can finish pricing approval.
[05:40] Aisha: Okay noted. Let's talk about specific redlines. Priya, can you list the top 5 items now?
[05:45] Priya: Sure: 1) indemnity cap adjustment; 2) subprocessor notice 30 days; 3) no-training clause explicit in DPA; 4) audit right scoped to SOC2 plus one annual remote attestation; 5) data residency clause enforcing EU-only storage for specified data sets.
[06:01] Aisha: We'll produce a redline with options for each item.
[06:05] Liam: For the pilot environment — technical ask — Jonas, what throughput and latency envelope will you test?
[06:12] Jonas: We want to replicate production-ish traffic: 50 concurrent sessions, median latency target <200ms 95th percentile, and test mixed short/long sequences for embeddings and chat.
[06:24] Liam: That's doable on a dedicated pool; we'll size the pilot, provide recommended GPU config and a monitoring board for token costs and latency.
[06:34] Rachel: Cost modeling — are there ways to cap spend during the pilot? We don't want runaway token costs.
[06:40] Aisha: Yes, we can set per-route quotas and show the estimated cost at different QPS. We'll include an estimator in the pilot quote.
[06:48] Jonas: Also need to confirm egress fees — if data is transferred between regions, what's the charge policy?
[06:53] Liam: Egress follows cloud provider fees plus a small pass-through; we'll call out expected egress scenarios in the quote. For region-pinned dedicated it should be minimal.
[07:05] Priya: For the DPA, we also require notification timelines for security incidents and a defined SLA for breach notification (e.g., 72 hours).
[07:13] Aisha: Our standard is 72 hours for incident notification; we can confirm in the DPA.
[07:18] Rachel: Anything else on SSO? We use SAML with SCIM for provisioning; we need role mappings and audit logging of admin actions.
[07:26] Liam: We support SAML and SCIM; RBAC can map to NovusHealth roles. Audit logging for admin actions is part of the console — we can provision longer retention for logs as an add-on.
[07:37] Rachel: Ok good.
[07:39] Aisha: Let's surface blocking items that would prevent procurement sign-off: 1) legal DPA/MSA redlines agreed; 2) pilot pricing SKU that procurement signs; 3) KMS/SSO integration plan; 4) SOC2 docs delivered. Anything else?
[07:52] Jonas: Proof of key isolation and key usage logs, otherwise security blocks.
[07:56] Priya: And the explicit no-training clause in the DPA.
[07:59] Aisha: Noted. We'll action those.
[08:02] [08:05] Speaker 3: (typing) Aisha posted a link to our standard DPA template.
[08:10] Aisha: I'll share a redline with three options for the indemnity cap: 1) mutual cap equal to 12 months fees, 2) mutual cap equal to 24 months fees, 3) carve-out for willful misconduct. Pick one and we'll file it for legal approval.
[08:23] Priya: We'll review and respond with preference.
[08:26] Rachel: On pricing approver — I'll need the procurement spreadsheet and the finance approver name.
[08:30] Aisha: I'll include the finance approver line in the quote.
[08:34] Liam: Technical note — for the dedicated pilot we can enable a limited debug window where you can run in production-like conditions with masked logging. That reduces risk.
[08:44] Jonas: Masked logging and no PII in logs is acceptable.
[08:48] Priya: One small question — is there an export control clause around certain model outputs? We need to ensure the MSA doesn't inadvertently permit restricted uses.
[08:57] Aisha: Good call. We'll add an export-control clause and align with your legal team's template.
[09:03] Rachel: Can we get an initial version of the pilot quote and the redline before the end of week? That would help move procurement.
[09:10] Aisha: Yes, we'll aim to deliver both by 2026-05-21.
[09:15] Priya: And let's set the legal-to-legal call for 2026-05-20 at 14:00 UTC unless you prefer another time.
[09:22] Aisha: That works for us; we'll propose the invite.
[09:25] Liam: I'll bundle the SOC2 summary, network diagram, and the KMS integration notes into one zip and share the link.
[09:33] Jonas: Also send the cipher suites and TLS termination details.
[09:36] Liam: Will do.
[09:38] Aisha: Anything else before we wrap?
[09:40] Rachel: No, that's it. Thanks.
[09:42] Aisha: Great, recap of next steps: redline MSA and DPA, pilot pricing quote, SOC2 + KMS docs, schedule legal call on 5/20. We'll add action owners in CRM.
[09:55] Priya: Thanks all.
[09:57] Meeting end.
